title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is part of the 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', which continues the Longue Marche. Grothendieck studies the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, which is free profinite on two generators. The generators ρ and σ are the inertia (loop) generators at two cusps, and ω is the third, with a relation of the type ρσω = 1. The 'équation des lacets' (loop equation) is the condition on automorphisms that later appears as one of the defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (Drinfeld, Ihara). Grothendieck works with variants attached to quotients 𝔖^+ of this group (or to the corresponding coverings), with:
- a distinguished subgroup L_0^𝔖;
- groups Z_{ρ,σ}, N_ρ, N_σ, G_{ρ,σ};
- 'Teichmüller-type' groups M_{ρ,σ}, which are extensions 1 → G^+ → SoM_{ρ,σ} → SoΓ_{ρ,σ} → 1.

What the previous page sets up. Given a (ρ,σ)-morphism between two such data (𝔖, 𝔖^φ) → (𝔖', 𝔖'^φ), the standard construction gives compatible homomorphisms φ_Z, φ_G (equations 93–95). Hence the whole diagram (64) attached to (ρ,σ) maps to the analogous diagram for (ρ',σ').

The Remark (completed on this page). Suppose 𝔖' has the following lifting property. For every pair α', β' in 𝔖'^𝔖_ε satisfying the loop relation (96), [α',ρ] = [β',σ]·ε_1^{μ-1} with μ ∈ Ẑ, there is an automorphism u' of 𝔖'^+ such that:
- u'(ρ) = α'(ρ) and u'(σ) = β'(σ) (equation 97);
- equivalently, α'^{-1}u' centralises ρ and β'^{-1}u' centralises σ (equation 98).

On this page Grothendieck adds that, in terms of u', the loop relation (96) becomes the condition u'(L_0^{𝔖'}) = L_0^{𝔖'} (equation 99), i.e. u' normalises 𝔖'. Under this hypothesis, every (ρ,σ)-morphism (𝔖, 𝔖^φ) → (𝔖', 𝔖'^φ) is automatically 'admissible'.

In modern terms: when every solution of the loop equation on the generators ρ and σ extends to a global automorphism, the extra compatibility condition ('admissible') in the definition of morphisms comes for free. This is analogous to the fact that, for the free profinite group, a pair (λ, f) determining the images of the generators defines an automorphism exactly when the GT-type relations hold.

He then announces that he will make this explicit in the universal case (the free profinite group itself). First, though, he will introduce the subgroups M(ω), M(ρ), M(σ) ⊂ M_{ρ,σ}. The next page defines these: they are the images in M_{ρ,σ} of three section subgroups of SoM^♮_{ρ,σ}, cut out by the conditions U = i_Z(u), U = i_ρ(a), U = i_σ(b). Each maps isomorphically onto SoΓ_{ρ,σ}. They play the role of decomposition-type stabilisers attached to the three cusps.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The equivalence 'loop relation (96) ⇔ u' normalises L_0^{𝔖'}' is only asserted, not proved, on this page. Equation (99) contains a notational slip: it states u'(L_0^{𝔖'}) = L_0^{𝔖'}, but the gloss says 'u' normalise 𝔖'' rather than L_0^{𝔖'}.

ideas.what: Loop equation (équation des lacets) linking pairs (α',β') acting on the inertia generators ρ and σ, with an exponent μ ∈ Ẑ
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon / 2-cycle type relations defining the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT-hat
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) for the program
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (sketched only); the detailed 'lacets' notes are unpublished

ideas.what: Criterion: if every solution of the loop equation lifts to an automorphism u' with prescribed images of ρ and σ, then every (ρ,σ)-morphism is admissible
ideas.modern_name: Automatic compatibility / lifting criterion for morphisms of GT-type data on finite quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution; related to work on finite quotients and the GT 'shadows' (Pop, Lochak–Schneps, Dolgushev)

ideas.what: Subgroups M(ω), M(ρ), M(σ) of M_{ρ,σ}, defined as images of section subgroups attached to the three cusps
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition/stabiliser subgroups of cusps inside GT-type extensions

missed.claim: A criterion stating that admissibility of morphisms between quotient (ρ,σ)-data is automatic once loop-equation solutions lift to automorphisms normalising L_0. This is a minor technical lemma inside the unpublished 'équation des lacets' framework. It loosely parallels later work on GT-shadows on finite quotients (Dolgushev and coauthors), but it is not a substantial new result.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of marginal interest for the finite-level approach to GT-hat (GT-shadows), where conditions under which morphisms of quotient data are automatically compatible matter.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short technical remark and transition inside the larger unpublished 'lacets' framework. Its content is a routine automatic-admissibility criterion. The announced subgroups are defined on the next page.
transcription_corrections: 'Nous allons expliquer ceci' reads more likely as 'Nous allons expliciter ceci'.
'tout ce qu'il faut [?] [?]' likely reads 'tout ce qu'il faut ici'.
The first line reads 'la relation des Lacets (96) s'exprimant en termes de u' par la condition', with u' rather than u.
